text:
sara: Quick post — I ran a focused perf sweep to understand where p95/p99 tail pain is coming from (prefill vs decode split) and have a concrete proposal. TL;DR: prefill dominates p95 on long prompts, decode dominates p99 tail under KV-miss churn.

perf-bot: benchmark summary attached for redwood-13b / a100-pool / seq=1024 gen=256 / microbatching ON
perf-bot: profile: prefill p50=120ms p95=420ms p99=780ms; decode p50=6ms/token p95=150ms p99=760ms (incl. KV miss spikes)

mike: surprised to see decode p99 so high — is that KV miss + kernel fallback?

julia: looks like it. I inspected traces: when KV cache miss rate > 5% we see large spikes where decode falls back to the slower matmul path and also triggers kernel rebinds.

kevin: can you paste the hot trace? small snippet is fine.

perf-bot: hot trace snippet:
```
# timeline (ms)
0-180  prefill: tokenization + prefix matmul kernel (cuBLAS_fast)
180-480 prefill: multihead attention fused kernel (opt_v3)
480-520 synchronous KV materialize (cache miss fallback)
520-860 decode: first token slow path (kernel swap to generic)
860-920 repeated rebinds due to mixed-precision fallthrough
```
```
KV miss rate: 6.2% (sampled 10k requests)
Kernel switches: 3 per-request on avg during tails
```

andrew: so two distinct pain points: (A) prefill cost for long contexts and (B) decode tail due to KV churn + kernel switch thrash. Right?

sara: yup. My read: for customer workloads with large prompts (>=1024) prefill is the dominant p95 contributor. But the p99 is mostly decode when the KV cache isn't sticky. If we make caching more consistent and reduce kernel switches, p99 comes down a lot.

mike: actionable ideas?

sara: proposal with prioritization: 
1) Quick wins (1–2 days):
 - instrument per-request KV hit/miss in tracing so we can correlate with kernel switches (add simple header: X-KV-hit-rate).
 - limit automatic kernel rebinds during decode: add a debounce window (200ms) before switching to a new kernel path.
 - lower Decode microbatch cap for low-latency tiers (microbatch=4 default), keep higher for throughput tiers.
2) Mid-term (1–2 weeks):
 - adaptive splitpoint: if prefill_time_estimate > 50% SLO, split prefill into sub-batches to smooth p95. If decode tail probability high, prioritize decode tokens scheduling.
 - KV cache admission: prefer longer-lived prefixes in LRU; reduce eviction churn on hot prefixes.
3) Research (2–4 weeks):
 - specialized decode fast-path that avoids rebinds when seq_len < 128 and kv_hit_rate > 90%
 - microkernel for small-MQ attention when cache grows beyond threshold

julia: I can ship the tracing header and KV-hit metrics today. Will add a quick dashboard: kv_hit_rate histogram by model and route.

kevin: debounce kernel rebind sounds low-risk. Do we have any tests that exercise frequent rebinds?

andrew: we have synthetic bench that purposely toggles dtype prefs per-request, but not a good proxy. We should create a mini-fuzzer that simulates interleaved requests with different seq_len and dtype to reproduce thrash.

mike: microbatching note: for prefill heavy workloads, larger microbatches improve throughput but push p95 up. We should add an explicit per-route hint: prefer_latency|prefer_throughput and default microbatch sizes accordingly.

sara: agreed. Suggested defaults: prefer_latency -> microbatch=4, prefer_throughput -> microbatch=12, default -> auto with SLO budget. We can evaluate with svc-level A/B.

perf-bot: rough estimated impact from earlier sims:
 - debounce rebind: p99 decode drop ~25%
 - KV-hit improvement + admission: p99 decode drop ~40%
 - prefill sub-batching: p95 prefill drop ~30% at cost of ~5% throughput drop

julia: I'll add the X-KV-hit-rate header + dashboard and run a 48h sample on prod canaries.

kevin: I'll implement the 200ms kernel rebind debounce and the microbatch per-route config. I'll also add a unit test that simulates 2000 requests with randomized seq_len to assert rebinds < 0.5 per-request on avg.

andrew: I'll build the fuzzer and run against staging; will attach reproducer if I hit the thrash pattern.

mike: plan looks good. One extra ask: include a small perf regression guard in prefill kernel changes — when we change matmul kernel heuristics, auto-rollback if p95 increases >5% in canary.

sara: noted. Action items summary:
 - julia: add X-KV-hit-rate + dashboard (ETA: EOD)
 - kevin: debounce rebind + per-route microbatch config + tests (ETA: 2d)
 - andrew: fuzzer & staged runs (ETA: 3d)
 - mike: add canary guard for kernel heuristic changes (ETA: 1d)
 - sara: run A/B microbatch (4 vs 8 vs 12) on dedicated canary once infra ready (ETA: 2d)

julia: sgtm :thumbsup:
kevin: will start on debounce PR now :rocket:
andrew: starting fuzzer. will ping with reproducer.

sara: thanks all — goal is to hit 2x p99 reduction for heavy decode tails without regressing throughput more than 8%. I'll post results here.
